answer_1.quote: Text style transfer (TST) aims to generate a text exhibiting a desired style based on the source text ... applications of TST cover a wide range of user‑centric natural language generation tasks, such as personalized dialogue systems, educational platforms, and writing assistants.
datasets: Stylized story dataset (Chinese: LuXun, JinYong, Fairy Tale; English: everyday stories and Shakespeare)

answer_2.quote: We employ BLEU1 and BLEU2 to evaluate the content preservation ... we employ the BERT Score metric ... we use two metrics for the overall performance ... the geometric means of Acc_d and BLEU (G‑BL_d ), and Acc_d and BS F1 (G‑BS_d ).
automatic_metrics: Geometric mean of Acc_d and BLEU (G‑BL_d)
Geometric mean of Acc_d and BERTScore F1 (G‑BS_d)

answer_4.quote: We randomly select 100 samples from the Chinese test set ... three Chinese native speakers are assigned the task of scoring for style polarity (Sty), content preservation (Con), and fluency (Flu), using a scale of 1 (very bad) to 3 (very good).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each generated text on style polarity, content preservation, and fluency using a 1‑3 Likert scale.
